neighbours.label: descriptive natural-science prose about plants and the environment (leaves turning colours, aerosols, distillation)
fire: In October the oak leaves fade from green to brown and gold.
The fern's compound leaves unfold slowly in early spring.
Sulphate aerosols in the stratosphere reflect sunlight back to space.
Lavender oil is obtained by steam distillation of the flowers.
The birch leaves turned yellow and fell in the first frost.
Each leaflet of the ash has a finely toothed edge.
Smoke particles and aerosols drifted across the valley for weeks.
The maple's broad leaves blaze orange before they drop.
quiet: In October the shop windows fill with brown and gold decorations.
The fern-patterned wallpaper was hung slowly in early spring.
Satellites in orbit send signals back to stations on the ground.
Lavender soap is sold at the market near the station.
The birch table turned yellow with age in the old kitchen.
Each chapter of the book has a short summary at the end.
Rumours and gossip drifted across the village for weeks.
The maple desk was polished before the guests arrived.
